question: The Sarpanch or the president of the Gram Panchayat is elected by the ward members as per the State Act for a period of ________ years.
solution:
The correct answer is __**5 years**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Sarpanch or the president of the Gram Panchayat is elected by the ward members as per the State Act for a period of **5 years**.
 
• Gram Panchayat is the basic unit of local self-government in rural India.
 
• The election process is governed by the respective State Election Commission, ensuring democratic governance at the grassroots level.
 
• The Sarpanch plays a crucial role in the administration of the village, implementing development programs and addressing the needs of the villagers.
 
• The tenure of 5 years allows for continuity and stability in the local governance and development initiatives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Gram Panchayat system was introduced through the **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992**, which aimed to decentralize power and enhance grassroots democracy.
 
• Each Gram Panchayat covers a village or a group of villages and is responsible for local administration and development.
 
• The Panchayati Raj system is a three-tier structure comprising the Gram Panchayat at the village level, the Panchayat Samiti at the block level, and the Zila Parishad at the district level.
 
• The Sarpanch is assisted by a team of elected Panchayat members, ensuring collective decision-making and administration.
 
• The Gram Sabha, consisting of all registered voters in the village, is the supreme body that oversees the functioning of the Gram Panchayat.
 
• The Sarpanch and Panchayat members are accountable to the Gram Sabha, which meets regularly to discuss and approve the village's development plans and activities.
